text:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — ran a 2h perf run on the continuous-batcher with a region-aware spill policy (EU primary, US secondary). Observed unexpected p99 inflation for EU-origin short-context requests once cross-zone spill exceeded ~8%.

Mira Patel: ugh. numbers?

Alex Chen: paste from profiler: 
[perf-summary] workload=chat-short seq=64
p50=14ms p95=96ms p99=378ms cross-zone-p99=812ms
cross-zone-rate=0.12 avg-batch=3.2 tokens/batch
KV-hit-rate-EU=0.71 KV-hit-rate-US=0.33

Jon Ortega: interesting — KV-hit drop in US is expected, but why does EU p99 go up when spill hits ~8%? that suggests some blocking or kernel mismatch when a few requests route out.

Sasha Ilyin: hypothesis: small batches are hitting a different kernel path (low-latency kernel) locally, but when we spill, those requests join batches with different seq distribution and trigger fallback kernel selection that increases per-token time. Also KV-cache misses amplify startup cost.

Mira Patel: can you dump the kernel-selection trace for a few cross-zone evts?

Alex Chen: pasted trace for req 8421/8424: 
----trace----
batch_id=5843 origin=eu1 spilled_to=us-west
local_batch_shape=[3 x 64] selected_kernel=fast_attention_v2
post-spill_merge_shape=[6 x 64] selected_kernel=fallback_attention_generic
kernel_switch_overhead=9.2ms
kv_fetch_first_token=12.8ms
----end----

Jon Ortega: that kernel switch + kv cold fetch sums up. If we keep affinity for small-reqs, they avoid merge. Maybe adjust affinity_window_ms and token_budget_target to discourage spill for short sessions.

Mira Patel: propose experiment: two arms for next 4h run.
A) Strict-affinity: affinity_window_ms=120, max_spill_pct=0.03, token_budget_target=1200
B) Soft-prefetch: affinity_window_ms=40, max_spill_pct=0.12, token_budget_target=2000 + aggressive kv-prefetch on spill handoff
Metrics: p50/p95/p99 per-region, median kernel_switch_overhead, per-token-cost (est).

Sasha Ilyin: Add one more tweak for B: when we spill, mark requests as "prefer-local-kv" and trigger async kv-warm for predicted next-token ranges. Might reduce first-token penalty.

Alex Chen: sounds good. I can flip traffic 50/50 via rollout policy. Will tag dedicated runs with meta:exp=affinity-vs-prefetch.

ci-bot: profiler-run-snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/exp/2071234567/trace.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

Jon Ortega: two quick asks before we run: 1) add a microbenchmark that measures kernel_selection latency for merged vs non-merged batches (same total tokens, varying shapes) 2) instrument per-request tag that records whether request hit local KV warm cache within 10ms of start.

Mira Patel: yep will add those metrics. Also put a soft guard that if EU p99 degrades >15% we auto-fallback to strict-affinity.

Sasha Ilyin: long-term thought: can we teach kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernel for mixed-shape merges if majority of requests in batch have seq<=64? might avoid the fallback. But that's a bit of engineering.

Alex Chen: agreed. For now we'll run the two arms and collect traces + kernel selection histograms. Rolling at 11:30 UTC. I'll post results after 4h. :rocket:

Mira Patel: thanks — excited to see if kv-prefetch buys us the permissive spill economics without tail regressions. :thinking:

Alex Chen: posted follow-up plan doc in #eng-runtime with config snippets and CI job ids.

ci-bot: experiment started: rollout_id=exp-2071234567-1 traffic_split=50/50
